body.statement:
Does there exist a total synthesis algorithm which, for every exactly encoded rational \(T\), \(\alpha\), compact \(\mathcal K\), and \(\varepsilon>0\), chooses finite \(K\) and rational \(h\) and returns a finite certificate \(\Gamma\) with \(\operatorname{Verify}(\iota,\Gamma)=1\)? Every accepted output must consist of finitely many rational polyhedral observable and nuisance cells, total endpoint-grid policy tables, and outward-rounded Poisson tail and enclosure data; acceptance must imply a measurable deterministic connected-interval family honest for every \(s\in\mathcal S_T\), every \(\kappa\in\mathcal K\), and every maintained nuisance value, together with
\[
 b_\varepsilon\le\overline D_{\mathrm{det}}(\mathcal K)\le U_\varepsilon,
 \qquad 0\le U_\varepsilon-b_\varepsilon\le\varepsilon.
\]
The lower object must be a finite-support integer program accompanied by a complete exact branch-and-bound proof, not an unresolved linear relaxation. This specialized exact-certificate question is not answered by Schafer and Stark (2009): their Theorem 2 concerns Monte Carlo risk convergence, whereas their Theorem 6 gives an off-support density-ratio risk bound. Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020), Section 2, gives qualitative drifting-subsequence criteria rather than a finite cover, computable enclosures, or a machine-checkable acceptance predicate. Because those papers use different models and action classes, no strict-strengthening or class-inclusion claim is made.
body.justification: The residual theorem-level question is whether exact fixed-design certificates can be synthesized uniformly over every observed share and every intensity in an arbitrary compact range, including zero-margin contacts.
body.gap: Schafer and Stark (2009), Theorem 2, proves Monte Carlo risk convergence, and their Theorem 6 gives an off-support density-ratio risk bound; neither yields a terminating continuum-honesty verifier or complete integer lower proof. Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020), Section 2, gives qualitative drifting-subsequence criteria rather than a finite rational-polyhedral certificate.
body.consumer: A positive answer would let auditors synthesize and replay exact-rational sparse-count confidence certificates simultaneously over the full observed-share simplex and any declared compact intensity range.

obligation.what_is_open: A terminating synthesis theorem for arbitrary rational inputs and compact intensity ranges must turn the finite closed profile-validity cover into finitely many rational-polyhedral observable cells, including every zero-margin coverage and target-endpoint contact.
obligation.obstruction: Fixed-design exponential--polynomial separation terminates for strict rational comparisons, but at an equality contact interval refinement alone does not determine a uniformly valid side. The resulting profile-validity boundaries can be curved, and no finite rational-polyhedral refinement with one valid total table per cell has been proved.
obligation.attempted: Finite action-profile enumeration, compact nuisance optimization on target-membership strata, algebraic critical-component representatives, outward count-tail and endpoint error bounds, and the closed-cover Borel-selector reduction solve strict-margin and fixed-design cases. The explicit early-kill theorem also shows that neither observed-share uniformity nor integrality alone is the remaining obstacle.
obligation.partial_result:
For fixed \(K\) and \(h\), let \(\mathcal A\) be the finite set of complete endpoint-grid profiles and, for \(a\in\mathcal A\), define
\[
 \mathcal R_a(r)=\left\{(s,\kappa)\in\mathcal S_T\times\mathcal K:
 \inf_{\nu}q_a(s,\kappa,\nu)\ge1-\alpha,
 \quad
 \sup_{\nu}r_a(s,\kappa,\nu)\le r
 \right\}.
\]
Upper semicontinuity of coverage, continuity of risk, and compactness of the nuisance box make every \(\mathcal R_a(r)\) closed. A pointwise endpoint-grid policy of risk at most \(r\) exists exactly when
\[
 \mathcal S_T\times\mathcal K=\bigcup_{a\in\mathcal A}\mathcal R_a(r),
\]
and choosing the first valid profile gives a Borel selector. At each fixed algebraic \((s,\kappa)\), strict coverage and risk comparisons reduce to the finitely many exponential--polynomial critical components already established, and the finite-profile argument supplies an exact finite nuisance witness set for the integer optimum. Separately, the proved early-kill theorem constructs an accepted globally share-uniform certificate at \((T,\alpha,\kappa,K,h,\varepsilon)=(3,1/20,1/100,2,1/100,1/20)\), with \(U_\varepsilon=5/2\), \(b_\varepsilon=49/20\), and a complete integer lower tree. The only residual question is whether the closed profile-validity cover over an arbitrary compact intensity range always admits a terminating finite rational-polyhedral refinement at zero-margin coverage and target-endpoint contacts.
